Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Phoenix Suns big man Khaman Maluach put his size to good use, at the expense of Houston Rockets forward Jabari Smith Jr., during an NBA Cup matchup between West Group A teams at the Toyota Center in Houston. The former Duke Blue Devils star center Maluach put Smith on a poster with a powerful two-handed throwdown and even drew a foul. Here is a look at that play. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) OH MY MAN MAN 😳 pic.twitter.com/25iiNdIa6c — Phoenix Suns (@Suns) November 26, 2026 That dunk capped an excellent two-man play between Maluach and Suns star shooting guard Devin Booker. After Booker refused the screen from Maluach, the big man simply rolled to the basket and was rewarded for his great off-the-ball movement with a nice pass from Booker. By the time Smith reacted, it was too late to stop Maluach from punishing the rim. More than Maluach’s dunk, the way the Suns set up that play was quite a delicious watch for basketball fans. At 7-foot-2 and just 20 years old, Maluach is still oozing with promise. He’s barely scratched the surface of his potential, and the Suns must be excited to see what kind of player he becomes as he continues to gain experience in the pros. Interestingly, the Rockets selected Maluach 10th overall in the first round of the 2025 NBA Draft before packaging him in a trade to the Suns that sent future Basketball Hall of Famer Kevin Durant to Houston. In his first 16 games in the 2026-27 NBA season, Maluach averaged 7.7 points, 5.6 rebounds and 0.9 blocks, while shooting 63.3 percent from the field. top.title: Chad Smith wears Wu-Tang Nikes to meet group; Lions unveil Wu merch
top.description: Chad Smith showed up for soundcheck at Ford Field for his Thanksgiving performance with the Wu-Tang Clan wearing Wu-Tang branded Nike Dunks, the Lions showed in an Instagram video released Nov. 25. Smith, the Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer who grew up in Bloomfield Hills, is set to join the Wu during their halftime performance during the Lions-Bears game on Nov. 26. The performance is curated by Eminem and Paul Rosenberg, who are in their second year of a three-year agreement to steer the Thanksgiving halftime show. More: Eminem's manager, Paul Rosenberg, calls Wu-Tang halftime 'a bullseye' In the video, Smith is seen greeting members of the Wu-Tang Clan, the legendary New York rap collective that was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame earlier this month. Smith is complimented on his kicks, a pair of black and yellow Nike Dunk high-tops branded with the Wu-Tang logo. The shoes were originally released in extremely limited edition in 1999, and were rereleased in 2024 for their 25th anniversary. "I'm representin', oh yeah!" Smith says, before Wu-Tang's Method Man says to the camera, "now who else can hang out with a Chili Pepper?" View this post on Instagram Wu-Tang was announced as the halftime performer on Nov. 1 . Paul Rosenberg, Eminem's manager, told The Detroit News the selection of Wu-Tang is "a bullseye" in terms of what he and Eminem want for the show. "When the idea of Wu-Tang came up, we just all thought A) it's going to be really unexpected, which we love, and B) we thought it was a bullseye for the right sort of association with the thing that Marshall and myself are passionate about, which his hip-hop," he said . "The idea of a Wu-Tang Thanksgiving seems so awesome that we went for it." Smith was announced as a guest performer with the Staten Island group on Nov. 20 . "Obviously Chad being from Michigan and being a huge Lions fan, it just made sense, and the band loved the idea as well," Rosenberg said. The Lions also unveiled several specialized Wu-Tang merch items that will be available at Thursday's game. They include a Wu-Tang Lions shirt (which reads "Shaolin to the Motor City" on the back), a Wu-Tang Forever T-shirt with a Lions logo at the center, and a Wu-Tang/ Lions crossover hoodie and crew neck sweatshirt. (To see the items, scroll to slide 5 in the post below.) View this post on Instagram The Wu-Tang/ Lions merchandise will be available at the game at Lions Supply inside Gate A, according to the Instagram post. top.title: Nets topple Bucks in NBA Cup clash to snap five-game skid
top.description: The teams with the two worst records in the Eastern Conference faced each other Wednesday night in Milwaukee, but no one needed to accuse either the Nets or the Bucks of tanking in this one. Neither team can win the draft lottery after the season because both franchises essentially traded their respective 2027 first-round picks years ago, but the Nets at least halted their five-game losing streak with a defensively improved 104-97 victory in an NBA Cup game at Fiserv Forum. Julius Randle netted a team-high 28 points as the Nets (4-13) posted their first NBA Cup victory after losses earlier in the season against the Pistons and the Magic. Michael Porter Jr. was held to 12 points on 4-for-14 shooting with 11 rebounds to follow another quiet scoring night (11) Monday in Minnesota. Julius Randle, who scored a team-high points, shoots a floater during the Nets’ 104-97 win over the Bucks on Nov. 25, 2026, in Milwaukee. Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Egor Dëmin had an active game with 14 points and a plus-15 rating in 25 minutes off the bench. Noah Clowney nailed three 3-pointers among his 17 points, and Day’Ron Sharpe contributed 11 points, 14 boards and five assists for the Nets. Tyler Herro, who had a career-best 50-point game Saturday against the 76ers, scored 21 of his 28 points in the second half for the Bucks (2-17). “We’ve lost a few in a row, so we’ve gotta try to get a win no matter who we’re playing against,” Porter told the YES Network before the game. “They’re an NBA team. They are at the bottom of the standings right now, but so are we, so it’s gonna be a dogfight, and we gotta try to get out of here with a win.” The NBA instituted rule changes in the offseason to discourage tanking for draft position, essentially penalizing the teams with the worst three records in the league with lower odds to secure the No. 1 overall pick in the lottery. The Nets’ 2027 first-round pick is controlled by the Rockets from an unprotected pick swap as part of Brooklyn’s deal to acquire James Harden in January 2021. The Bucks, who dealt away superstar forward Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Heat over the summer, also had committed to a pick swap involving their 2027 first-rounder when they acquired guard Jrue Holiday from New Orleans in 2020. The Nets had allowed at least 70 points in the first half four times during their five-game skid, but this slow start was more due to offensive inefficiency. Noah Clowney, who scored 17 points off the bench, puts up a shot during the second quarter of the Nets’ road win over the Bucks. Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Brooklyn missed five of its first six shots and spotted the Bucks a 9-2 lead in the first three minutes. But Porter knocked down two straight 3s and scored eight as part of a 15-1 run to vault the Nets into an eight-point advantage en route to a 28-24 edge through 12 minutes. top.description: Long before he reached the global stage, Kongklai Sor Sommai had already mastered the art of the comeback. He lost the first 10 bouts of his career, then rattled off 18 straight wins. Back-to-back defeats are hardly the deepest hole he has climbed out of, and his next turnaround begins against fellow Thai Worapon Lukjaoporongtom in the bantamweight Muay Thai co-main event of The Inner Circle 40 on Friday, November 27. The card goes down live in Asia primetime from Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium, exclusively for members at live.onefc.com . Stoppages of Ferrari Fairtex and Mohammad “Prince of Persia” Habibpour bookended a hard-fought win over Kendu Irving , giving him three consecutive victories and his best run in ONE. Then came a pair of painful setbacks. Julio Lobo outpointed him at The Inner Circle 12 in May, before Adam “El Capitano” Benwarwar survived two knockdowns to stop him in the second round at The Inner Circle 22 in July. Looking back on both losses, Kongklai admits his eagerness to entertain sometimes got the better of him. In the weeks since, he has worked to close the gaps in his armor. The Sor Sommai slugger told onefc.com: “For this camp, my team focused extra attention on my defense because my opponent is also a southpaw with a dangerous high kick. “I keep reminding myself not to get careless or repeat the same mistakes. Coming off a 2025 season in which they were one win away from making it to the World Series for the first time in franchise history, they struggled during all of 2026 and missed the postseason entirely after winning just 76 games. And while the biggest problem point for the Mariners is their offense, that should not preclude them from making improvements to the other parts of the roster. In fact, they have been looking to improve their bullpen immensely with the signing of Adrian Morejon. top.title: Timberwolves Lose Another Star to Injury
top.description: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Timberwolves came off a long stretch at home to travel to Oklahoma City on Thanksgiving Eve for an NBA Cup game against the Thunder. Chris Finch’s team entered at 13-5, including 4-2 on the road, and had won its first two Group B games in the NBA Cup . Despite their playoff struggles against the Thunder, the Wolves came away with the win. Moving to 3-0 in NBA Cup play came at a cost. Already without Anthony Edwards and Donte DiVincenzo , Minnesota could now be without LaMelo Ball too. LaMelo Ball hurts ankle late for MN Timberwolves Minnesota came out strong against the Thunder, racing out to a 26-16 lead . The Wolves gave it back in the second quarter but responded in the second half and down the stretch. Then, with 2:29 left, LaMelo Ball rolled his left ankle after landing on Isaiah Hartenstein’s foot. LaMelo Ball grabbing left ankle and needs to be helped off the floor. He’s in a LOT of pain. — Jon Krawczynski (@JonKrawczynski) November 25, 2026 Finch didn’t have an update after the game. “It looked pretty bad but I’m not sure,” Finch said, according to Alan Horton (Wolves Radio) . Before the injury, Ball had played 29 minutes , scoring 19 points on 7-of-18 shooting with seven rebounds and eight assists while running the offense. He had played in all 19 games for Minnesota. He played 72 games last year but averaged just 35 per season in the three years before that. Related: Two Key Timberwolves Added to Injury Report The MN Timberwolves have looked for a facilitating point guard since Ricky Rubio left. Ball is the best mix of star power and prime-age talent they have had at the position since then, and he has kept Finch’s rotation afloat without DiVincenzo and Edwards. If the ankle injury isn’t significant, Ball may not miss much time. While he’s out, Ayo Dosunmu should get plenty of run at the point, and DiVincenzo’s return becomes even more important. Penn State football has a new quarterback on board for the 2027 recruiting class, as three-star prospect Ben Rolapp flipped his commitment to the Nittany Lions from Boston College, On3’s Hayes Fawcett reported Wednesday night. His addition gives Penn State a new pledge at the position after losing its previous quarterback commit, Will Wood, to the Eagles last month. Wood initially committed to the Nittany Lions in May before switching to Boston College in late October. His connection with Eagles head coach Bill O’Brien, who previously led Penn State, played a role in that decision. The Nittany Lions subsequently pursued Missouri commit Braylen Warren, with head coach Matt Campbell traveling to Omaha, Nebraska, during the team’s bye week to extend an offer in person. However, Warren decided to remain with the Tigers, forcing Penn State to explore other options. The Nittany Lions eventually turned their attention to Rolapp, extending him an offer on October 28. The Connecticut native had originally committed to Boston College in June after attending a camp with O’Brien and his coaching staff. His decision to visit Penn State on November 22-23 came shortly after Brunswick School completed its undefeated season. top.title: No. 2 Ludlowe completes its first unbeaten regular season with victory over rival Warde
top.description: Fairfield Ludlowe quarterback Ryan Love runs for a touchdown in the second half against Fairfield Warde on November 24, 2026. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut M) FAIRFIELD - The Ludlowe football team finished what no Falcons squad had before it - an unbeaten regular season - with a 28-15 win over rival Warde on Wednesday night, earning one of the top two seeds in the upcoming Class L playoffs. The Falcons (10-0) have now qualified for the state tournament three straight years, but will host a CIAC playoff game as the higher seed for the first time in program history and attempt to earn the school's first postseason win. "10-0 means the world to me. I have been working with these kids since first grade and started playing tackle in fifth grade," Ludlowe quarterback Ryan Love said. "To see the whole town come together for a game is just bigger than football. Even if they are wearing red, it's a great atmosphere and I am so grateful I got to play in this game." More than 3,800 fans packed Taft Field to watch Ludlowe earn its seventh straight win in the series and keep the Gallagher/Banyas Trophy with the Falcons. Warde leads the all-time series 17-15. "Who would have thought 10 years ago, when I took the job and was told outright that we would never be .500?" Ludlowe coach Mitch Ross said. "It has been a lot of work, but it has been a labor of love. I love the players, love the coaches and they put everything into it." Ludlowe, ranked No. 2 in the GametimeCT Top 10 Football Poll, will be one of the top two seeds in the Class L tournament, where it lost in the quarterfinals in each of the past two seasons. It will have to wait for the result of Naugatuck's game Thursday before knowing its seed and opponent. "We will never forget that we have never won a playoff game here," Love said. "We haven't proved anything in the postseason and I know this team can prove a lot this postseason. I think we can make a run. The sky is the limit for this team." Warde was eliminated from playoff contention with the loss, but finished 6-4 in the first season under coach Steve Christy. "I am just so proud of this team," Christy said. "The senior class has set the stage for us. The way we fought today. We easily could have fallen over, but I thought we showed a lot of guts." Ludlowe led 14-0 at halftime on touchdown passes from Love to Timmy O'Neil and Jackson Danylko, then took a 21-0 lead in the third quarter on a 16-yard run from Love. Warde got on the board in the third on a pass from Luke Mancuso to AJ Cortina. Love ran for another touchdown from 34 yards out in the fourth quarter, and the scoring was capped by Warde's Dylan Osserman's 3-yard run. top.title: Jannik Sinner ruled out of Australian Open as injury lay-off continues
top.description: FILE PHOTO - Italian tennis player Jannik Sinner looks at the ball during his men's singles first-round match against Germany's Yannick Hanfmann at the Terra Wortmann Open tennis tournament. (is associated with: «Jannik Sinner ruled out of Australian Open as injury lay-off continues») David Inderlied/dpa Jannik Sinner will miss the Australian Open after undergoing knee surgery. The world number two has not played since defending his Wimbledon title in July and will now miss the first Grand Slam tournament of 2027. Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo said in a statement: "We've been in regular touch with Jannik's team and they've confirmed he won't be joining us for the Australian Open in January following his recent surgery. "Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for the Australian Open in 2028." The Italian confirmed on Tuesday he had undergone minor surgery after experiencing ongoing pain in his right knee. Sinner said in a statement earlier this week: "Over the past few months, together with my team, we've tried everything to treat my injury without surgery. "After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn't respond as we had all hoped, that's why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band. "I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team." The iliotibial band is a thick band of fibrous connective tissue running down the outside of the thigh, and injuries associated with it are typically caused by overuse. Prior to his injury, the 25-year-old had a stellar start to 2026 which saw him win the first five Masters 1000 tournaments of the year, becoming the second man after Novak Djokovic to achieve the Golden Masters. His absence has allowed Alexander Zverev to overtake him in the world rankings, with Carlos Alcaraz in third place. Both men shared their well-wishes after Sinner's surgery. "The decision of making the surgery, I think his team made a good decision. He's young, has a lot of years ahead of him. I'm sure he's going to come back even stronger, even better," Alcaraz said on Wednesday. Zverev added: ""We know that he's mentally strong. I hope that he takes every step serious and that, in three, four months' time, he can be back to 100 per cent and be back playing."

top.title: College basketball expert calls Mark Pope a ‘major disappointment’
top.description: Kentucky Basketball is off to a disappointing start to the 2026-27 season, and the criticism surrounding Mark Pope and his program continues to grow following consecutive losses to Kansas by 20 points and Indiana by 14 points. NBC Sports college basketball analyst John Fanta recently shared his thoughts on the state of Kentucky basketball, and he didn’t hold back when discussing the third year of the Pope era. “Let’s just call it what it is: the Mark Pope era, to this point, has been a disappointment,” Fanta said. Fanta questioned Kentucky’s defensive scheme, physicality, and overall roster construction, pointing to the Wildcats’ struggles to stop opposing teams throughout the early portion of the season. “Their defensive scheme, I’m not sure what it is. Scheme would be an exaggeration for what it actually is. They couldn’t stop anybody early in the season. They couldn’t stop Northern Arizona. They weren’t going to stop Indiana. Milan Momcilovic, a winning player at a winning program, a lot is now on his shoulders. Too much is on his shoulders for a team with the kind of money that they possess. Their guards, not sturdy enough, not physical enough,” Fanta said. He also questioned whether Kentucky has the type of players necessary to meet the program’s traditional expectations. “When I think of Kentucky, I think of enforcers. They’re not that. I like Malachi Moreno, but I look at this Kentucky roster, and I compare it to the resources that they are reported to have available. Mark Pope is not getting it done there.” Fanta continued his criticism by pointing to the expectations that come with coaching at Kentucky and the amount of money reportedly invested in the roster. “To me, it comes off as he’s trying to be someone that he actually isn’t at a very difficult job. It’s a hard job because they have high expectations, but you are judged on your record,” he continued. “They had to claw just to get past Santa Clara in the NCAA Tournament with a $20 million roster. They spent a ton of money again. They’re not getting it done.” Fanta ultimately believes Kentucky may need to make a change if things don’t turn around, calling the current state of the program a major disappointment. “The Mark Pope era is a major disappointment, and Kentucky is going to have to make a change. … It’s just a brutal start to their season, and that fanbase has every right to be upset because, at Kentucky, if you want to be categorized as a blue blood—which the playing field has been level—it’s a very, very big disappointment.” With Kentucky now facing increased pressure following its losses to Kansas and Indiana, Pope and the Wildcats have plenty of work to do to get the season back on track.

Against Washington and Ole Miss, BYU shot just 11 of 51 (22%) from 3-point range, with Cougar players not named Collin Chandler providing just five of those makes. For a tournament famous for being very shooter-friendly, Kevin Young’s crew certainly wasn’t seeing any sunny results. But the soft rims of the Lahaina Civic Center finally came to BYU’s aid on Wednesday, as the Cougars defeated the Providence Friars thanks to 17 made 3-pointers. Considering the 85-82 final score, BYU needed every last one of those triples. The Cougars’ 38 attempts from beyond the arc set a new single-game Maui Invitational record, and the 17 makes tied the 2014 Cougars for the event’s second-highest mark. Somewhere out there, Chase Fischer is smiling. “It was more of a BYU-style win, I would say,” Young told reporters postgame. “That was a big message coming in. We wanted to try to impose our will in terms of how we want to play and not be so reactive, which I thought we did a good job of that.” After going silent offensively in the second half of Tuesday’s loss to Ole Miss, the Cougars bounced back in a major way against Providence and its top-15 rated defense, as they torched the Friars for 1.32 points per possession and 19 assists on 28 made field goals. Providence was surrendering just 64 points per game before Wednesday. nigeria.title: Nigeria Joins Global Pact To Protect Marine Biodiversity, Unlock Ocean Resources
nigeria.description: Nigeria has secured a significant international milestone for the country’s marine and blue economy, following its formal ratification of a landmark United Nations treaty on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. The historic instrument of ratification was deposited on behalf of President Bola Tinubu by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. ﻿ Speaking at the ceremony, Ibrahim highlighted the economic and strategic importance of the agreement to Nigeria, noting that it would expand the country’s opportunities to benefit from ocean resources through greater participation in the governance of the high seas. The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for the protection, management and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries. A major implication of the ratification is Nigeria’s plan to develop a proposal for the establishment of a highly protected marine area on the high seas. The initiative is also expected to strengthen efforts to conserve marine ecosystems while promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits from ocean resources, particularly for developing countries. Nigeria signed the BBNJ Agreement on May 3, 2024. Following the deposit of its instrument of ratification, the agreement will enter into force for Nigeria on December 24, 2026. This will enable the country to participate as a full Party at the first Conference of the Parties, scheduled to open on January 11, 2027. At the ceremony, Ibrahim acknowledged Evelyn Campos Sanchez, Officer-in-Charge of the United Nations Treaty Section, for receiving Nigeria’s instrument of ratification. Nigeria’s commitment to the agreement is further reinforced by the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, alongside the adoption of a National Blue Economy Policy and a national roadmap for implementing the treaty. As a party to the agreement, Nigeria will continue to advocate for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from marine genetic resources and digital sequence information. The country will also push for stronger capacity-building initiatives and the transfer of marine technology to African and other developing nations. Ambassador Ibrahim further noted Nigeria’s support for the establishment and effective operation of a Special Fund with adequate and predictable resources to enable developing countries to implement the agreement. nigeria.title: 4 African countries to have produced Miss Universe winners
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African contestants have earned the Miss Universe crown six times, across four countries. South Africa leads with three wins, while Namibia, Botswana and Angola have each won once. The titleholders claimed their crowns between 1978 and 2019, giving each country a place in the pageant’s history. The latest milestone achieved by an African nation is from Miss Universe 2024 where Nigeria’s Chidimma Adetshina finished as first runner-up and was named Miss Universe Africa and Oceania. That was a notable result for Nigeria, but it did not add another country to the list of African Miss Universe winners as the overall crown went to Denmark’s Victoria Kjær Theilvig. Here are the four African countries ranked by the number of Miss Universe crowns their representatives have won. South Africa: three wins South Africa has won the title three times. Margaret Gardiner became the country’s first winner in 1978. Demi-Leigh Nel-Peters won in 2017, and Zozibini Tunzi followed in 2019. Tunzi was the third South African winner and the first Black South African woman to earn the crown. Namibia: one win Michelle McLean won Miss Universe in 1992, becoming the first and, according to the pageant’s official profile, so far the only Namibian woman to win. The win came two years after Namibia gained independence in 1990. Botswana: one win Mpule Kwelagobe won the title in 1999. She remains the only woman from Botswana to be crowned Miss Universe, according to the pageant’s official legacy page. Angola: one win Leila Lopes won Miss Universe in 2011, becoming the first Angolan titleholder. The official Miss Universe legacy page records her win and notes that she later served as national director of Miss Angola Universe. nigeria.title: Gordon hits brace as Barcelona cruise to 4-1 Sabah win

Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus also found the net for the Spanish champions as they triumphed in Azerbaijan at the Baku Olympic stadium. The Catalan giants were without teenage star Lamine Yamal for the long journey east, but found their rhythm after a slow start to claim the three points and a fourth win from five matches in the Champions League. Despite Yamal’s absence, Barca coach Hansi Flick also chose to rest Raphinha, handing Jesus a rare start up front since his summer move from Arsenal. Khayal Aliyev fired a good early chance straight at Joan Garcia as Sabah threatened in attack, against Barca’s notably fragile defence. Barca midfielder Pedri was denied at the other end before Sabah hit the crossbar, with Ivan Lepinjica’s looping effort beating Garcia but not the woodwork. Gordon broke the deadlock in the 31st minute after Sabah goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov pushed Adeyemi’s cross into his path. The England international netted four goals in his prior appearance in Baku, against Qarabag for Newcastle last season, and was Barca’s brightest player. Gordon had a second effort ruled out for offside against Jesus in the build-up, before the interval. The winger struck six minutes into the second half after Jesus’s effort was saved and the rebound came his way. It was the first of three goals in 10 minutes for the Catalan giants, with Adeyemi notching after Alejandro Balde crossed for him. Jesus bundled home Barca’s fourth of the night from almost on the goalline after Pokatilov parried Jules Kounde’s header. Barcelona had kept a clean sheet against Aston Villa in their previous European clash, after conceding in the previous 18, but were unable to add another. Joy-Lance Mickels pulled one back for Champions League debutants Sabah with a cool finish after Christian Nwachukwu pulled the ball across for him. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor A bill that would write the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law is now eligible for a vote on the House floor, after the House Financial Services Committee formally reported it on Tuesday. The American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, H.R. 8957, was filed with amendments as House Report 119-894 and placed on the Union Calendar as Calendar No. 789 on Nov. 24, according to congressional records. The committee had voted 28-21 to advance the bill at a Sept. 16 markup. Rep. Nick Begich, an Alaska Republican, introduced the bill on May 21. It now lists 23 cosponsors, including Rep. Jared Golden, a Maine Democrat, with Reps. Byron Donalds and Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida added on Nov. 24. What the amended bill does The reported text directs the Treasury secretary to set up a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a separate Digital Asset Stockpile within 180 days of the law taking effect. Bitcoin owned by the federal government would move into the reserve, while other digital assets would go to the stockpile. The centerpiece is a lock-up. Treasury would have to hold all bitcoin deposited in the reserve for at least 20 years after enactment, and during that period no reserve bitcoin could be “sold, swapped, auctioned, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of for any purpose.” After the 20 years, the Treasury secretary could recommend selling up to 10% of the reserve in any two-year period. Two years before the holding period ends, Treasury would have to send Congress recommendations on whether to keep holding or begin a gradual release. Federal agencies would have 60 days after enactment to give Treasury a full accounting of the bitcoin and other digital assets they hold or have seized. Until the reserve is set up, agencies could not sell those coins except for national security, when required by law or a court, or to return assets to crime victims. The bill also creates a Proof of Reserve system. Treasury would publish an annual report on total holdings, transactions and control of private keys, checked by an independent auditor with expertise in cryptographic attestations, while the Government Accountability Office would provide oversight. States could choose to store their own bitcoin in segregated accounts inside the federal reserve, keeping title to the coins and the right to withdraw them. Changes from Begich’s original version The committee rewrote the bill before reporting it. Begich’s introduced text asked Treasury and Commerce to study funding bitcoin purchases with surplus remittances from Federal Reserve Banks or a revaluation of the Fed’s gold certificates, as well as with tax payments, tariff revenue and gifts. Those options are gone from the amended study, which now looks at swapping other digital assets in the stockpile, forfeitures and settlements, and partnerships with states or private entities. entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. sports.description: Chad Smith showed up for soundcheck at Ford Field for his Thanksgiving performance with the Wu-Tang Clan wearing Wu-Tang branded Nike Dunks, the Lions showed in an Instagram video released Nov. 25. Smith, the Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer who grew up in Bloomfield Hills, is set to join the Wu during their halftime performance during the Lions-Bears game on Nov. 26. The performance is curated by Eminem and Paul Rosenberg, who are in their second year of a three-year agreement to steer the Thanksgiving halftime show. More: Eminem's manager, Paul Rosenberg, calls Wu-Tang halftime 'a bullseye' In the video, Smith is seen greeting members of the Wu-Tang Clan, the legendary New York rap collective that was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame earlier this month. Smith is complimented on his kicks, a pair of black and yellow Nike Dunk high-tops branded with the Wu-Tang logo. The shoes were originally released in extremely limited edition in 1999, and were rereleased in 2024 for their 25th anniversary. "I'm representin', oh yeah!" Smith says, before Wu-Tang's Method Man says to the camera, "now who else can hang out with a Chili Pepper?" View this post on Instagram Wu-Tang was announced as the halftime performer on Nov. 1 . Paul Rosenberg, Eminem's manager, told The Detroit News the selection of Wu-Tang is "a bullseye" in terms of what he and Eminem want for the show. "When the idea of Wu-Tang came up, we just all thought A) it's going to be really unexpected, which we love, and B) we thought it was a bullseye for the right sort of association with the thing that Marshall and myself are passionate about, which his hip-hop," he said . "The idea of a Wu-Tang Thanksgiving seems so awesome that we went for it." Smith was announced as a guest performer with the Staten Island group on Nov. 20 . "Obviously Chad being from Michigan and being a huge Lions fan, it just made sense, and the band loved the idea as well," Rosenberg said. The Lions also unveiled several specialized Wu-Tang merch items that will be available at Thursday's game. They include a Wu-Tang Lions shirt (which reads "Shaolin to the Motor City" on the back), a Wu-Tang Forever T-shirt with a Lions logo at the center, and a Wu-Tang/ Lions crossover hoodie and crew neck sweatshirt. (To see the items, scroll to slide 5 in the post below.) View this post on Instagram The Wu-Tang/ Lions merchandise will be available at the game at Lions Supply inside Gate A, according to the Instagram post. Kickoff for Thursday's game is scheduled for 1:02 p.m. agraham@detroitnews.com This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Chad Smith wears Wu-Tang Nikes to meet group; Lions unveil Wu merch

sports.title: Nets topple Bucks in NBA Cup clash to snap five-game skid
sports.description: The teams with the two worst records in the Eastern Conference faced each other Wednesday night in Milwaukee, but no one needed to accuse either the Nets or the Bucks of tanking in this one. Neither team can win the draft lottery after the season because both franchises essentially traded their respective 2027 first-round picks years ago, but the Nets at least halted their five-game losing streak with a defensively improved 104-97 victory in an NBA Cup game at Fiserv Forum. Julius Randle netted a team-high 28 points as the Nets (4-13) posted their first NBA Cup victory after losses earlier in the season against the Pistons and the Magic. Michael Porter Jr. was held to 12 points on 4-for-14 shooting with 11 rebounds to follow another quiet scoring night (11) Monday in Minnesota. Julius Randle, who scored a team-high points, shoots a floater during the Nets’ 104-97 win over the Bucks on Nov. 25, 2026, in Milwaukee. Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Egor Dëmin had an active game with 14 points and a plus-15 rating in 25 minutes off the bench. Noah Clowney nailed three 3-pointers among his 17 points, and Day’Ron Sharpe contributed 11 points, 14 boards and five assists for the Nets. Tyler Herro, who had a career-best 50-point game Saturday against the 76ers, scored 21 of his 28 points in the second half for the Bucks (2-17). “We’ve lost a few in a row, so we’ve gotta try to get a win no matter who we’re playing against,” Porter told the YES Network before the game. “They’re an NBA team. They are at the bottom of the standings right now, but so are we, so it’s gonna be a dogfight, and we gotta try to get out of here with a win.” The NBA instituted rule changes in the offseason to discourage tanking for draft position, essentially penalizing the teams with the worst three records in the league with lower odds to secure the No. 1 overall pick in the lottery. The Nets’ 2027 first-round pick is controlled by the Rockets from an unprotected pick swap as part of Brooklyn’s deal to acquire James Harden in January 2021. The Bucks, who dealt away superstar forward Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Heat over the summer, also had committed to a pick swap involving their 2027 first-rounder when they acquired guard Jrue Holiday from New Orleans in 2020. The Nets had allowed at least 70 points in the first half four times during their five-game skid, but this slow start was more due to offensive inefficiency. Noah Clowney, who scored 17 points off the bench, puts up a shot during the second quarter of the Nets’ road win over the Bucks. Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Brooklyn missed five of its first six shots and spotted the Bucks a 9-2 lead in the first three minutes. But Porter knocked down two straight 3s and scored eight as part of a 15-1 run to vault the Nets into an eight-point advantage en route to a 28-24 edge through 12 minutes. A 3-pointer by Clowney and a jumper by Randle extended the cushion to 10 early in the second. The Nets led by as many as 13 before the Bucks closed

Back-to-back defeats are hardly the deepest hole he has climbed out of, and his next turnaround begins against fellow Thai Worapon Lukjaoporongtom in the bantamweight Muay Thai co-main event of The Inner Circle 40 on Friday, November 27. Then came a pair of painful setbacks. Julio Lobo outpointed him at The Inner Circle 12 in May, before Adam “El Capitano” Benwarwar survived two knockdowns to stop him in the second round at The Inner Circle 22 in July. Looking back on both losses, Kongklai admits his eagerness to entertain sometimes got the better of him. In the weeks since, he has worked to close the gaps in his armor. sports.title: Timberwolves Lose Another Star to Injury
sports.description: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Timberwolves came off a long stretch at home to travel to Oklahoma City on Thanksgiving Eve for an NBA Cup game against the Thunder. Chris Finch’s team entered at 13-5, including 4-2 on the road, and had won its first two Group B games in the NBA Cup . Despite their playoff struggles against the Thunder, the Wolves came away with the win. Moving to 3-0 in NBA Cup play came at a cost. Already without Anthony Edwards and Donte DiVincenzo , Minnesota could now be without LaMelo Ball too. LaMelo Ball hurts ankle late for MN Timberwolves Minnesota came out strong against the Thunder, racing out to a 26-16 lead . The Wolves gave it back in the second quarter but responded in the second half and down the stretch. Then, with 2:29 left, LaMelo Ball rolled his left ankle after landing on Isaiah Hartenstein’s foot. LaMelo Ball grabbing left ankle and needs to be helped off the floor. He’s in a LOT of pain. — Jon Krawczynski (@JonKrawczynski) November 25, 2026 Finch didn’t have an update after the game. “It looked pretty bad but I’m not sure,” Finch said, according to Alan Horton (Wolves Radio) . Before the injury, Ball had played 29 minutes , scoring 19 points on 7-of-18 shooting with seven rebounds and eight assists while running the offense. He had played in all 19 games for Minnesota. He played 72 games last year but averaged just 35 per season in the three years before that. Related: Two Key Timberwolves Added to Injury Report The MN Timberwolves have looked for a facilitating point guard since Ricky Rubio left. Ball is the best mix of star power and prime-age talent they have had at the position since then, and he has kept Finch’s rotation afloat without DiVincenzo and Edwards. If the ankle injury isn’t significant, Ball may not miss much time. While he’s out, Ayo Dosunmu should get plenty of run at the point, and DiVincenzo’s return becomes even more important. sports.title: No. 2 Ludlowe completes its first unbeaten regular season with victory over rival Warde
sports.description: Fairfield Ludlowe quarterback Ryan Love runs for a touchdown in the second half against Fairfield Warde on November 24, 2026. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut M) FAIRFIELD - The Ludlowe football team finished what no Falcons squad had before it - an unbeaten regular season - with a 28-15 win over rival Warde on Wednesday night, earning one of the top two seeds in the upcoming Class L playoffs. The Falcons (10-0) have now qualified for the state tournament three straight years, but will host a CIAC playoff game as the higher seed for the first time in program history and attempt to earn the school's first postseason win. "10-0 means the world to me. I have been working with these kids since first grade and started playing tackle in fifth grade," Ludlowe quarterback Ryan Love said. "To see the whole town come together for a game is just bigger than football. Even if they are wearing red, it's a great atmosphere and I am so grateful I got to play in this game." More than 3,800 fans packed Taft Field to watch Ludlowe earn its seventh straight win in the series and keep the Gallagher/Banyas Trophy with the Falcons. Warde leads the all-time series 17-15. "Who would have thought 10 years ago, when I took the job and was told outright that we would never be .500?" Ludlowe coach Mitch Ross said. "It has been a lot of work, but it has been a labor of love. I love the players, love the coaches and they put everything into it." Ludlowe, ranked No. 2 in the GametimeCT Top 10 Football Poll, will be one of the top two seeds in the Class L tournament, where it lost in the quarterfinals in each of the past two seasons. It will have to wait for the result of Naugatuck's game Thursday before knowing its seed and opponent. "We will never forget that we have never won a playoff game here," Love said. "We haven't proved anything in the postseason and I know this team can prove a lot this postseason. I think we can make a run. The sky is the limit for this team." Warde was eliminated from playoff contention with the loss, but finished 6-4 in the first season under coach Steve Christy. "I am just so proud of this team," Christy said. "The senior class has set the stage for us. The way we fought today. We easily could have fallen over, but I thought we showed a lot of guts." Ludlowe led 14-0 at halftime on touchdown passes from Love to Timmy O'Neil and Jackson Danylko, then took a 21-0 lead in the third quarter on a 16-yard run from Love. Warde got on the board in the third on a pass from Luke Mancuso to AJ Cortina. Love ran for another touchdown from 34 yards out in the fourth quarter, and the scoring was capped by Warde's Dylan Osserman's 3-yard run. sports.title: Jannik Sinner ruled out of Australian Open as injury lay-off continues
sports.description: FILE PHOTO - Italian tennis player Jannik Sinner looks at the ball during his men's singles first-round match against Germany's Yannick Hanfmann at the Terra Wortmann Open tennis tournament. (is associated with: «Jannik Sinner ruled out of Australian Open as injury lay-off continues») David Inderlied/dpa Jannik Sinner will miss the Australian Open after undergoing knee surgery. The world number two has not played since defending his Wimbledon title in July and will now miss the first Grand Slam tournament of 2027. Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo said in a statement: "We've been in regular touch with Jannik's team and they've confirmed he won't be joining us for the Australian Open in January following his recent surgery. "Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for the Australian Open in 2028." The Italian confirmed on Tuesday he had undergone minor surgery after experiencing ongoing pain in his right knee. Sinner said in a statement earlier this week: "Over the past few months, together with my team, we've tried everything to treat my injury without surgery. "After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn't respond as we had all hoped, that's why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band. "I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team." The iliotibial band is a thick band of fibrous connective tissue running down the outside of the thigh, and injuries associated with it are typically caused by overuse. Prior to his injury, the 25-year-old had a stellar start to 2026 which saw him win the first five Masters 1000 tournaments of the year, becoming the second man after Novak Djokovic to achieve the Golden Masters. His absence has allowed Alexander Zverev to overtake him in the world rankings, with Carlos Alcaraz in third place. Both men shared their well-wishes after Sinner's surgery. "The decision of making the surgery, I think his team made a good decision. He's young, has a lot of years ahead of him. I'm sure he's going to come back even stronger, even better," Alcaraz said on Wednesday. Zverev added: ""We know that he's mentally strong. I hope that he takes every step serious and that, in three, four months' time, he can be back to 100 per cent and be back playing."

sports.title: College basketball expert calls Mark Pope a ‘major disappointment’
sports.description: Kentucky Basketball is off to a disappointing start to the 2026-27 season, and the criticism surrounding Mark Pope and his program continues to grow following consecutive losses to Kansas by 20 points and Indiana by 14 points. NBC Sports college basketball analyst John Fanta recently shared his thoughts on the state of Kentucky basketball, and he didn’t hold back when discussing the third year of the Pope era. “Let’s just call it what it is: the Mark Pope era, to this point, has been a disappointment,” Fanta said. Fanta questioned Kentucky’s defensive scheme, physicality, and overall roster construction, pointing to the Wildcats’ struggles to stop opposing teams throughout the early portion of the season. “Their defensive scheme, I’m not sure what it is. Scheme would be an exaggeration for what it actually is. They couldn’t stop anybody early in the season. They couldn’t stop Northern Arizona. They weren’t going to stop Indiana. Milan Momcilovic, a winning player at a winning program, a lot is now on his shoulders. Too much is on his shoulders for a team with the kind of money that they possess. Their guards, not sturdy enough, not physical enough,” Fanta said. He also questioned whether Kentucky has the type of players necessary to meet the program’s traditional expectations. “When I think of Kentucky, I think of enforcers. They’re not that. I like Malachi Moreno, but I look at this Kentucky roster, and I compare it to the resources that they are reported to have available. Mark Pope is not getting it done there.” Fanta continued his criticism by pointing to the expectations that come with coaching at Kentucky and the amount of money reportedly invested in the roster. “To me, it comes off as he’s trying to be someone that he actually isn’t at a very difficult job. It’s a hard job because they have high expectations, but you are judged on your record,” he continued. “They had to claw just to get past Santa Clara in the NCAA Tournament with a $20 million roster. They spent a ton of money again. They’re not getting it done.” Fanta ultimately believes Kentucky may need to make a change if things don’t turn around, calling the current state of the program a major disappointment. “The Mark Pope era is a major disappointment, and Kentucky is going to have to make a change. … It’s just a brutal start to their season, and that fanbase has every right to be upset because, at Kentucky, if you want to be categorized as a blue blood—which the playing field has been level—it’s a very, very big disappointment.” With Kentucky now facing increased pressure following its losses to Kansas and Indiana, Pope and the Wildcats have plenty of work to do to get the season back on track.

Considering the 85-82 final score, BYU needed every last one of those triples. The Cougars’ 38 attempts from beyond the arc set a new single-game Maui Invitational record, and the 17 makes tied the 2014 Cougars for the event’s second-highest mark. Providence was surrendering just 64 points per game before Wednesday. Speaking to reporters during a community back-to-school event in Miami on July 28, Adebayo revealed the message he sent James after learning of his decision. However, he first made sure to clarify that there were no hard feelings. “There ain’t no disappointment,” Adebayo said, per the Miami Herald. “To me, you should always be happy for a person and their decision. He made a decision where he feels like it’s his best situation to win. And I feel like I’m a good friend of LeBron’s.” The Heat star then revealed the playful warning he had delivered privately. “Like I told him in the message, I’m going to bust his a**,” Adebayo added. “So, it’s going to be an exciting season. SpaceX asked the FCC to waive its rule requiring the atmospheric disposal of dead satellites orbiting at 2,000 km or less. Elon Musk’s company asked for “flexibility to dispose satellites operating above 600 km altitude into Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” The FCC found SpaceX did not provide enough information to let it assess if proposed “alternative disposal methods” are compliant with regulations, so deferred its decision on the waiver request. “SpaceX must file an application for modification of this authorization and provide sufficient justification for any requested waiver(s) of the Commission’s rules,” the order states. The company must also file twice-yearly reports about “conjunction events” – moments when its satellites get dangerously close to each other, or other orbiters. Whether orbiting datacenters are feasible, make sense, or will ever pay for themselves, remain open questions. Analyst firm Gartner has described the idea as “ peak insanity .” Google thinks orbiting datacenters become viable if launch costs fall to $200/kg, which would mean SpaceX needs to launch its massive Starship 1,800 times. SpaceX’s assumptions assume near-daily launches, far better than its current cadence of a launch every three days or so. A new index, called Water Supply Chain Watch and published by exposure management firm Securin, however, found almost twice as many vulnerabilities as public records identified – including 20 exploited flaws that weren't even in the federal government's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The security provider compared data on water-tech vendors with records from the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the FBI, and WaterISAC, drawing on CISA advisory data through November 20 and KEV catalog entries through November 23. technology.title: Huawei and crew tout homegrown EDA tools to overcome China’s fab deficit
technology.description: Chinese telecom and IT giant Huawei boasted about its advancements in domestic electronic design automation (EDA) software this week, which it needs to accelerate the adoption of homegrown chip manufacturing. EDA is an umbrella term for software, hardware, and services essential to the planning, design, and production of modern chips. Today, Cadence Design Systems, Synopsys, and Siemens dominate the industry, but US export controls have restricted Huawei and other blacklisted Chinese businesses' access to their tools. The US blacklisted Huawei back in 2019 over concerns the telecommunications equipment giant could be forced to inject backdoors into its gear. Unable to access top EDA tools, Huawei’s chip division, HiSilicon, was forced to develop its own with the help of Phlexing Technology. This week, Phlexing chairman Qing He detailed the company’s efforts to bring new EDA tools to support Huawei’s so-called Tau Scaling Law design philosophy. “Tau EDA is the domestic EDA tool chain for Tau chips. It comes from a long, close partnership with Huawei,” he said. We discussed the tech earlier this year, but in a nutshell, it involves using advanced packaging, specifically 3D hybrid bonding, to achieve higher transistor density for a given area. The TSMC of China, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), is still years behind Taiwan, South Korea, and the US on process technology. It currently has the ability to mass-produce chips on the equivalent of a 7 nm process. For comparison, TSMC began producing 5 nm-class products in 2020 and commenced mass production of 2 nm-class chips in late 2025. So, Huawei aims to use 3D packaging to close the gap, but for this to happen, it first needs tools capable of designing such chips, and that’s just what Phlexing claims to have done with its GloryBolt and GloryEX platforms. “Traditional EDA has long handled only single processes. Tau EDA needs to integrate and decompose multiple processes,” He said. “Coupling multi-scale, multi-structure, and multi-physics issues called for new analysis tools.” This, He says, culminated in the co-development of a process design kit (PDK) with Huawei beginning in 2024. These technologies have now gone live. The development comes as Huawei looks to bring larger, more capable processors to market. We previously discussed the company’s latest developments around AI accelerators, near packaged optics, networking, and rack systems. Many of these advancements will depend on multi-die chip packages, enabled by EDA tools, like those built by Phlexing. ®

It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
science.description: null On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet. NASA's M2-F3 lifting body drops from its carrier plane during a test flight in 1970. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered In the late 1960s and early 1970s, NASA was investigating lifting bodies as an approach to both new aircraft and what future spacecraft, and as its number suggests, the M2-F3 was not the first of its kind. In fact, the M2-F3 was a rebuilt version of its predecessor, the M2-F2 lifting body , after that vehicle crashed in a dry lake bed in California's Mojave Desert during an unpowered test flight. That crash (which appears in the opening of the TV show "The Six-Million-Dollar Man") led to upgrades for a better handling lifting body, NASA said. "When the M2-F2 was rebuilt and redesignated the M2-F3, it was modified with an additional third vertical fin – centered between the tip fins – to improve control characteristics," NASA wrote in an overview . Unpowered glide flights for the M2-F3 began in June 1970, but Dana's flight on Nov. 25 of that year was the first time the vehicle fired up its rocket engine to test its controls under powered flight. One vital upgrade on the vehicle was a set of reaction control thrusters to help maintain its orientation. "A reaction jet control system, similar to thrusters used on orbiting spacecraft, was also installed on the M2-F3 to obtain research data about their effectiveness for vehicle control," NASA wrote . "As the M2-F3’s portion of the lifting body program neared an end, it evaluated a rate command augmentation control system and a side-arm control stick similar to side-arm controllers now used on many modern aircraft." If you want, you can see the M2-F3 vehicle today. NASA donated it to the Smithsonian Institution. It is now hanging at the National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Want more space history? science.description: A northern gannet ( Morus bassanus ) tagged with biologging devices on its back and tail Steve Votier Audio from seabirds fitted with mini recording devices and GPS trackers has been used by researchers to show that marine life can record encounters with vessels that are otherwise difficult to track. Many large vessels are now legally required to carry automatic identification systems broadcasting their identity and location at regular intervals. Although this has allowed interactions between animals and fisheries to be studied at scale, there are enormous gaps in coverage. In fact, recent research suggests that three-quarters of industrial fishing vessels don’t use the technology, says Jonathan Rutter at the University of Oxford. This is partly because regulations on the types of vessels that are required to share data vary by country. Large satellite ‘blind spots’ also contribute to the problem, he says, and so does subterfuge for the purpose of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (IUU). Advertisement Read more Most large fishing boats go untracked as ‘dark vessels’ Rutter says that being caught as bycatch in fishing is one of the greatest risks to seabird populations, but if fishing vessels are only tracked “with conventional methods, such footprints of risk may be strikingly incomplete”. The team analysed audio collected from devices attached to seven northern gannets ( Morus bassanus ) and found that one third of the audio detections couldn’t be matched with vessel tracking data – mostly off the UK coast. Overall, 12 per cent of the vessel detections made by the four critically endangered Balearic shearwaters ( Puffinus mauretanicus ) included in the study couldn’t be matched to public data. But given the high vessel density where they were – off the Catalan coast – the researchers estimated that up to 20 per cent of the vessels detected by the four birds weren’t broadcasting their identity. Tammy Davies at BirdLife International – a global partnership of non-governmental organisations – who wasn’t involved in the study, says the research could “give us a more complete picture of the risks seabirds face at sea” and “ultimately, this could contribute to better assessments of bycatch risk and help identify fisheries and areas where conservation measures are most needed”. science.title: Green light for Starmind: SpaceX gets approval to deploy 1 million AI satellites
science.description: null Earth orbit could get a lot more crowded in the coming years. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) just granted SpaceX approval to deploy one million of its Starmind AI data-center satellites in orbit. "This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said today (Nov. 25) in a statement announcing the approval. AI has become central to SpaceX's business plans and identity over the past year or so. For example, the company has said that it's eyeing a "total addressable market" of $28.5 trillion over the long haul — and nearly $23 trillion of that is in "enterprise AI applications." Starmind is key to those lofty ambitions. SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk believes that the future of AI compute is in space, where energy (from the sun ) is unlimited and there are no land-owning neighbors to lodge NIMBY complaints. SpaceX aims to launch the first of its Starmind satellites in the third quarter of 2027. The spacecraft will fly on the company's fully reusable Starship megarocket, which has deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink satellites on its most recent two test flights . Those 52 spacecraft are the vanguard of another enormous constellation: Musk has said that the next-gen Starlink network will eventually consists of about 100,000 satellites . The planned numbers for Starlink and Starmind are truly mind-boggling. To put them into perspective: Since the dawn of the space age in 1957, humanity has launched a total of just 28,000 satellites, give or take a few hundred. And the biggest constellation ever operated to date, the current iteration of Starlink, consists of about 11,000 spacecraft. These coming buildouts will require an enormous number of launches. Starship can carry a maximum of 60 V3 Starlink satellites per launch, for instance, so it will take about 1,700 liftoffs just to assemble that network (and more to maintain it, as the operational life of each satellite is expected to be about five years). Putting so many satellites into orbit also raises the risks of collisions. SpaceX has proven to be extremely proficient in this regard with its current Starlink satellites, which can detect and avoid potential collisions autonomously. But more evasive maneuvers will be required as space gets more and more crowded. SpaceX isn't the only company that aims to operate data centers in space; Cowboy Space , Starcloud, Blue Origin and Google, among other companies, have voiced similar ambitions. Starcloud and Google , in fact, have already launched AI pathfinder satellites. science.title: AI’s stunning progress in maths shows how little we understand it
science.description: MARK SYKES/SPL/Alamy There is a story, possibly apocryphal, that when the mathematician G. H. Hardy was about to undertake a dangerous sea voyage, he sent a postcard to a colleague declaring “I have solved the Riemann hypothesis”. Hardy, a staunch atheist, joked that this would prevent his ship from sinking, as God would never let him claim the credit for such a major result without revealing the details of his proof. Hardy would probably be both astonished and aghast that we now have what seems to be a proof of the Riemann hypothesis , a problem that has vexed mathematicians since the 19th century, but that no one yet understands it. The consensus among mathematicians is that the proof, produced with the aid of AI, will hold, but that it will take much more work to make it comprehensible to humans. However you feel about AI, this is a watershed moment, and one that demonstrates just how little we still understand about the capabilities of the technology. As recently as last month, leading mathematician Terence Tao speculated that AI would eventually solve the Riemann hypothesis, but that it may not happen before 2050. Now, some mathematicians are considering whether their hardest and most infamous remaining problems could be settled within months. In a year that has left mathematicians reeling, this may be the knock-out blow. Advertisement This is a watershed moment, and it shows just how little we understand about AI’s abilities For non-mathematicians, the fall of the Riemann hypothesis is harder to interpret. In the past year, AI has seen incredible advances in both maths and coding, but it is perhaps no coincidence that in these arenas, with nothing more than computer code, answers can swiftly be checked and iterated upon, allowing for rapid improvement. When it comes to other human endeavours though, from art to zoology, such verification is far harder, involving either the messy physical world, or unknowable human taste – or both. Whether this verification gap can be closed may become the biggest question of our age. Answers on a postcard, please. What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental? It has been called the hardest problem in mathematics, and now through a combination of human ingenuity and relentlessness, and the computational power of AI, the Riemann hypothesis may have finally been solved

Set on the planet Eden, a sunless world that drifts alone far outside the Milky Way, this follows the descendants of two astronauts who were marooned there over a century earlier. Now numbering 532 people, they tell each other stories of the world their ancestors came from, and struggle to survive on this dark, cold planet as they await the return of “one of those sky-boats with lights on them”. I think it is all wildly imaginative and original and exciting. So it was with some trepidation that I awaited the verdict of my fellow book club members on our Discord channel. science.title: Is The Time Traveler’s Wife the perfect audiobook to experience on shuffle?
science.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Reader Jenny Ozanne writes to tell us of a horrific incident that befell her partner. He had bought Audrey Niffenegger’s novel The Time Traveler’s Wife as a CD audiobook, to listen to on long car journeys. “After a while, he complained that the plot was completely impossible to follow,” writes Jenny. “It was only when I checked his player that I realized he had accidentally set the CD to ‘shuffle’. “ Advertisement Jenny raises two points, which Feedback heartily endorses: “I’m still not sure what’s more impressive: the story’s ability to survive total chronological chaos, or the fact that he listened to three random chapters before suspecting anything was wrong.” Feedback would suggest that The Time Traveler’s Wife might be the ideal novel to experience on shuffle, since the narrative is heavily non-linear. The main character hops uncontrollably back and forth through history. This led us to wonder: would any similarly chrono-displaced stories survive the experience of being played on shuffle, or even be improved by it? We wondered, for instance, about David Mitchell’s Cloud Atlas . This has six stories set in different periods, including a future in which human clones are used as cheap labour, and a more distant future in which everything has gone a bit Mad Max . The stories are linked by characters in later timelines reading about the earlier ones, and by subtle coincidences. What would it be like on shuffle? However, after careful reflection, we realised there is only one correct answer to this, and that is Shane Carruth’s 2004 film Primer , which tells the story of two tech bros who invent a time machine in their garage. At first, they use it to go back in time and make money on the stock exchange, only to become caught up in an escalating web of betrayal and deception as they endlessly rewrite their lives. Primer is so overcomplicated, so mind-wreckingly confusing, that some poor soul once went so far as to draw a diagram trying to convey its timeline. Posted on Reddit by u/Clawz114, the diagram looks like a cross between a metro map and a flowchart of the inner workings of a chemical factory. It is therefore possible that playing the scenes in random order might actually cause the film to make more sense. science.title: NASA Eyes Crop Candidates for Future Menus
science.description: As NASA prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition, and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can help with menus in deep space, something top of mind this week as the nation celebrates Thanksgiving. Strawberries (left) grown in the Space Life Sciences Lab’s controlled environment chamber. Cucumbers (center) and lemon basil (right) grown in a controlled environment chamber at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. NASA Recent testing points to strawberries, cucumbers, and lemon basil as potential options for future explorers. Space crops can absorb carbon dioxide, produce oxygen, and recycle water. These capabilities will become increasingly important as crewed missions extend farther from our home planet. While space crop research advances on Earth, capabilities are also expanding in space. A new investigation from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division is set to launch to the International Space Station, where the first-of-its-kind prototype growth chamber will provide critical insights for developing crop production systems that could grow crops like these for future Moon Base habitats and Mars missions. Sweet space strawberries Strawberries are among the few sweet fruits under consideration for spaceflight and are nutritious, aromatic, and self-pollinating. Researchers at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida are growing strawberries in flight-like growth chambers to evaluate the potential space crop, and NASA partners at The Australian Research Council Centre for Excellence in Plants for Space also are helping expand knowledge of space strawberries. Researchers at NASA Kennedy, the University of Melbourne, and the University of Western Australia recently tested a wild strawberry against NASA’s leading strawberry candidate, ‘Delizz,’ to see which thrived better under simulated space conditions. Delizz and the wild strawberry produced very different fruits, according to a study published in September in the journal Life Sciences in Space Research. Delizz grew large, red fruit, while the wild strawberry produced small, yellow fruit due to a recessive genetic mutation. But looks are not everything. When grown from a seed, the wild strawberry produced twice as many buds, flowers, and fruit as Delizz. Ultimately, however, NASA’s pick kept its top spot, as the wild strawberry grew too many runners that would take up valuable room aboard a spacecraft. science.title: Pakistani astronaut becomes 1st international visitor to China's Tiangong space station (photos)
science.description: null For the first time ever, a foreign astronaut has set foot inside China's Tiangong space station. That pioneer is Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who arrived at Tiangong aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft early this morning (Nov. 25). "The Chinese space station is always something to look forward to!" the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) wrote in an update today (in Mandarin; translation by Google). "China's 'Tiangong' welcomes partners from all over the world to visit!" Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces, is a payload specialist on Shenzhou-24. He found his way onto the mission thanks to a space-cooperation agreement that China signed with Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025 . Ali and his two Shenzhou-24 crewmates — commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi — enjoyed a short and smooth ride to their orbital destination. They lifted off atop a Long March 2F rocket on Tuesday (Nov. 24) at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT on Nov. 25) and reached Tiangong a little over six hours later. Tang and Wu will live aboard the outpost for the usual six-month stint. Ali, however, will come home in just a week, hitching a ride with two of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts, who arrived at Tiangong in May . Ali will be busy during his short space stay, conducting a set of joint Chinese-Pakistani experiments. "Four collaborative projects in biotechnology and materials are planned, with Ali also scheduled to conduct an in-orbit experiment involving photosynthetic cyanobacteria," The Times of India wrote today . The third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will remain on the station until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore set a Chinese record, becoming the first astronaut from his country to live in low Earth orbit for a full year. Astronauts from the Soviet Union/Russia and the United States have already blazed this long-duration trail. The global record for longest continuous space stay is 437 days, set by cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov aboard the Mir space station from January 1994 to March 1995. Another look at the Shenzhou-23 and Shenzhou-24 astronauts aboard Tiangong on Nov. 25, 2026. (Image credit: CMSA) Ali is not the first person from Pakistan ever to reach space, by the way. That distinction belongs to adventurer Namira Salim, who traveled to suborbital space on a tourism flight with Virgin Galactic in October 2023. Shenzhou-24 is the 12th crewed mission to Tiangong, a three-module, T-shaped outpost that China finished assembling in late 2022. Well, "finished" might not be the right term; China plans to expand Tiangong , which is currently about 20% as massive as the International Space Station .

science.title: Hera spacecraft gets 1st up-close look at stadium-sized hole punched in asteroid by NASA DART mission
science.description: null NASA's DART Earth-defense mission punched a stadium-sized hole in a distant asteroid, and we have seen it up close for the first time thanks to the Hera spacecraft. NASA's DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) mission made history on Sept. 26, 2022, when it slammed into Dimorphos , the small moonlet of the much larger asteroid Didymos . The mission tested if such an impact could be deployed to divert an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. Scientists have known for some time that this deflection attempt was successful; the system's orbit around the sun was lengthened by 33 minutes, but the European Space Agency's (ESA) Hera mission launched in October 2024 to travel the 120 million miles (194 million kilometers) to the Didymos system to observe the effect of the DART impact in greater detail. Now, the spacecraft has revealed that DART flattened one face of Dimorphos with a stadium-sized crater and set it tumbling chaotically. The impact also appears to have blasted out hundreds of previously unknown boulders that are now circling the binary asteroids. Her parents worked at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, and discussions about happenings at the agency continued even when they came home from the office. “I remember a poignant dialogue we had after the space shuttle Challenger disaster,” Knight recalled. “However, we talked just as much about the engaging work my parents were doing inside Goddard’s gates.” Her father Lyle Knight was a mechanical engineer, while her mother Julia Knight worked the bulk of her career in human resources. They brought their daughter on center for Take Your Child to Work Day and other events, and over time she became hooked. “I saw the chambers where spacecraft and instruments were being tested, as well as other facilities used to help further space exploration.
